root.claim: One deterministic Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes outputs $\operatorname{bin}_{2n}(\operatorname{val}(x)\operatorname{val}(y))$ for all $n$-bit inputs $x,y$ in time $T_A(n)=O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ with $\kappa=2^{-182}$, so the $n\log n$ optimality conjecture fails in this model.
root.method: Build two network-derived tape procedures that beat one pass per transform level, use them to compute convolution over $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ by synthetic transforms, reduce exact multiplication to that convolution through radix digits, a Chinese-remainder map, Gaussian resampling, chirps and a phase twist, then bound the error and sum the normalized costs.

motivation.text: In a transform-based multiplier, merely scanning the $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels costs $\Theta(n\log n)$, so going below $n\log n$ needs savings in both address movement and butterfly arithmetic; the reduction isolates exactly those two operations.

quote.quote: We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

root.salient: The saving $\kappa=2^{-182}$ in the exponent of $\log n$ is minute, but it is a genuine power saving, which is already enough to refute the $n\log n$ conjecture.

adds.name: logical volume
adds.meaning: The number of stored data bits of the array an operation acts on, excluding temporary work streams.

adds.name: working precision
adds.meaning: The number $6\lceil\log_2n\rceil$ of fractional bits of the fixed-point complex coefficients.

adds.name: axis count
adds.meaning: The number $\lfloor\lceil\log_2n\rceil^{\epsilon}\rfloor$ of transform axes, $\Theta(p^{\epsilon})$.

adds.name: record length
adds.meaning: The power of two $2^{\ell}$ giving the number of complex coefficients of each polynomial record in $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$.

adds.name: record exponent
adds.meaning: The exponent $\log_2r$, which also bounds the number of rounds of each synthetic transform.

adds.name: padded box size
adds.meaning: The power of two $\prod_it_i$ of complex entries in the padded transform array, with $Tp=\Theta(n)$.

adds.name: power-of-two axis length
adds.meaning: The length $r/2$ or $r$ of axis $i$ of the padded box.

adds.name: chunk width
adds.meaning: The number $\lfloor d^c\rfloor$ of address bits in each chunk on which a simultaneous layer selects one bit.

adds.name: interchange exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed exponent $1-2^{-50}$ in the address-interchange cost $O(Vu^{\tau})$.

adds.name: layer exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed exponent $1-2^{-54}$ in the simultaneous-layer cost $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$.

children.claim: Two fixed-tape procedures beat one pass per level: interchanging two disjoint contiguous $u$-bit address fields of an array costs $O(Vu^{\tau})$, and a normalized butterfly $H_0$ applied simultaneously to one selected bit in each of $D\le d$ equal $K$-bit address chunks costs $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$, with fixed $\tau,\lambda'<1$.
children.method: Build fixed linear networks that exchange two banks while restoring scratch values, give each wire a frame so that every edge change is a smaller call of the same procedure, and solve the resulting volume-normalized recurrences.

motivation.text: A network whose wires carry whole arrays turns one large operation into a fixed number of smaller instances of itself, so its cost obeys a recurrence, and well-chosen frames make every edge such an instance.

quote.quote: The intermediate frames are chosen so that every edge can be implemented by smaller calls to the same procedure.

adds.name: field width
adds.meaning: The number of address bits in each of the two interchanged fields.

adds.name: layer chunk count
adds.meaning: The number of address chunks whose selected bit receives a butterfly in one simultaneous layer.

children.claim: On an array of logical volume $V$ stored in lexicographic order, a fixed permutation of the digits at two radix-$q$ positions, moving one digit, splitting on a digit to apply a fixed pointwise map and merging back, and cyclically splitting whole rows into a fixed number of streams (and merging them) each cost $O(V)$ steps.

quote.quote: Each of the following operations on an array of volume $V$ takes $O(V)$ steps on a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes:

children.claim: If a target field $y\in[Q]$, $Q=q^b$, follows its control fields, the update $y\mapsto y+a(\text{controls})\bmod Q$ costs $O(V)$ whenever the offset is computable in $b^{O(1)}$ time, by splitting each fiber's $Q$ blocks at $Q-a$ and merging the two pieces in the opposite order; multiplying $y$ by a fixed rational unit also costs $O(V)$.

quote.quote: costs $O(V)$ if the offset can be prepared in $b^{O(1)}$ time from the fixed number of control values.

children.claim: Two fixed linear networks with $W$ wires each exchange two banks of $N$ values while restoring every scratch value, and their frame changes need in total only $s<Wm$ smaller calls on role streams of volume $V/W$, indeed $s/W<m^{\tau}$ with $\tau=1-2^{-50}$; so when the recursion parameter is multiplied by $m$ the volume-normalized cost is multiplied by less than $m^{\tau}$, a power saving.
children.method: Label every vertex of each network by a subspace of an $m$-dimensional space, count the dimension changes along edges, convert them into rational ranks (bit network) or orthonormal residual bases (complex network), and compare the total with $Wm$.

motivation.text: A recursion that replaces one call at parameter $mf$ by $s$ calls at parameter $f$, each on volume $V/W$, multiplies the normalized cost by $s/W$ per factor $m$; only a strict deficit $s<Wm$ makes this factor $m^{\tau}$ with $\tau<1$, so the exact count of edge ranks decides whether any saving exists.

quote.quote: This strict inequality is the source of the power saving.

children.salient: The relative deficit $1-s/(Wm)$ is minute (about $1.5\cdot10^{-11}$ for the bit network), yet any strict deficit already yields a power saving.

adds.name: wire count
adds.meaning: The number of wires (roles) of the network, scratch wires included, which is also the number of role streams the rows are split into.

adds.name: label dimension
adds.meaning: The dimension $100^3$ of the label space, which is also the number of digit fields or slots a chunk is cut into at each recursion level.

adds.name: total edge rank
adds.meaning: The number of smaller recursive calls the network's edges need: the sum of edge ranks or residual dimensions.

adds.name: bank size
adds.meaning: The number of index triples $a$, i.e. of values in each of the two exchanged banks.

adds.name: dimension loss
adds.meaning: The total label dimension lost along decreasing edges of the network.

children.claim: For arbitrary initial scratch values, a forward invocation of the eight-row schedule (copy, gather, scatter, side injection and their undoings) effects $y\gets y+x$, and a forward, an inverse and a forward stage send $(X_a,Y_a)\mapsto(-Y_a,X_a)$ while restoring every auxiliary wire; over $\mathbb F_2$ this is the bank exchange.
children.method: Track the old scratch vectors through the schedule, compute the net coefficient from each $x_T$ to $y_S$ from the size of $S\cap T$, and compose the three stages.

motivation.text: The schedule first cancels the effect of the unknown scratch contents and finally restores them, so the net effect is a fixed linear map that can be computed as if the scratch were zero; only its coefficients, which depend on triple intersections, remain to be checked.

quote.quote: The first two rows of the following schedule remove the effect of the old scratch values;

children.salient: The exchange is exact for arbitrary, unknown initial scratch values, so scratch roles can later be filled with genuine data rows instead of reserved blank space.

children.claim: With initial side and central vectors $a,c$, rows 0 and 1 subtract $\mathcal Ja+\mathcal Rc$, rows 2 to 5 add $\mathcal R(c+\mathcal Gx)+\mathcal J(a+\mathcal Vx)$ and rows 6 and 7 restore $a,c$, so the target changes by $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$ whatever $a,c$ are.

quote.quote: The net target change is $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$, independently of $a,c$.

children.claim: In the bit construction the central (gather then scatter) coefficient from $x_T$ to $y_S$ is $|S\cap T|\bmod 2$; the side wires cancel exactly the neighbours with $|S\cap T|=1$, triples meeting in $0$ or $2$ points already have coefficient $0$, and the self coefficient ($|S\cap S|=3$) is $1$, so the net map is $y\gets y+x$.

quote.quote: The side contribution cancels exactly the intersection-one cases; distinct triples with intersection zero or two already have coefficient zero, and the self coefficient is one.

children.claim: In the complex construction the central coefficient is $(|S\cap T|-1)/2$; the side wires cancel it for distinct triples meeting in $0$ or $2$ points, intersection one contributes $0$, and the self coefficient is $(3-1)/2=1$, so again $y\gets y+x$.

quote.quote: The side cancels it for distinct triples with intersection zero or two; intersection one contributes zero, and the self coefficient is one.

children.claim: Since the inverse schedule effects $X\gets X-Y$, the three stages take $(x,y)$ to $(x,y+x)$, then $(-y,y+x)$, then $(-y,x)$, and each invocation restores its own auxiliary wires.

quote.quote: Starting from $(x,y)$, the three stages give $(x,y+x)$, then $(-y,y+x)$, then $(-y,x)$.

children.claim: If each wire's scalar is replaced by an array on a common address set and each vertex $v$ gets an invertible frame $D_v$, shared by all incidences of a gate, with $D_vD_u^{-1}$ applied on each edge, then the pointwise network implements $D_{\rm out}\mathsf S_\Omega D_{\rm in}^{-1}$: a route from input role $w$ to output role $\rho(w)$ applies only $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$.
children.method: Maintain the invariant that the stored array at each vertex is its frame applied to the logical array, and verify it at sources, along edges and through gates.

motivation.text: A gate combines values at one address while a frame mixes addresses within one wire, so a shared frame commutes with the gate by linearity; hence intermediate frames telescope and can be chosen freely to make edges cheap.

children.claim: At a gate whose touched wires all carry frame $D_v$, linearity gives $\sum_jc_jD_v\varphi_j=D_v(\sum_jc_j\varphi_j)$, so the invariant passes through every gate to the sinks.

quote.quote: Thus the common frame commutes with the pointwise gate, and the invariant continues to the sinks.

children.claim: Consequently, for a signed role permutation, every route, auxiliary roles included, applies its sign times the endpoint operator $D_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$, and the intermediate frames are free.

quote.quote: Once the scalar routing is fixed, the endpoint frames determine the array operator on each route; the intermediate frames can then be chosen to make each edge change inexpensive.

children.claim: Each vertex can be labelled by a nondegenerate subspace of $\mathcal F=F^{\otimes3}$, of dimension $m$, so that the labels on every edge are nested and the absolute label-dimension changes over all edges sum to $Wm-2N+2L$, where the dimension $L$ lost on decreasing edges satisfies $L/N=100/539$ (bit network) or $101/539$ (complex network), both below $1/2$.
children.method: Build labels from tensor products of indicator lines of three-element subsets of $[100]$, verify nesting along each edge from the orthogonality of neighbouring triples, and telescope the signed dimension changes at the gates.

motivation.text: Neighbouring triples have orthogonal indicator lines in the chosen bilinear form, so one triple's line fits inside the other's orthogonal complement; this lets almost every edge only enlarge its label, confining all losses to the central wires.

quote.quote: Orthogonality of the corresponding indicator vectors permits the subspace assignments.

children.claim: For the form $\langle x,y\rangle=x^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)y$ on $\mathbb Q^{100}$ (nondegenerate, eigenvalues $1$ and $-91/9$) indicator vectors of triples satisfy $\langle t_S,t_T\rangle=|S\cap T|-1$ and $\langle t_T,t_T\rangle=2$, and over $\mathbb F_2$ the dot product gives $t_T\cdot t_T=1$ and $t_S\cdot t_T=|S\cap T|\bmod2$; so triple lines are nondegenerate and neighbouring ones orthogonal in either label field.

quote.quote: Thus every triple line is nondegenerate, and neighboring triple lines are orthogonal, in the label field belonging to either construction.

children.claim: The terminal labels are $U_a=\langle u_a\rangle$ at source $X_a$ and $0$ at every other source, and $\mathcal F$ at sinks $X_a$ and scratch, $U_a^\perp$ (dimension $m-1$) at sinks $Y_a$; so the source dimensions sum to $N$ and the sink dimensions to $Wm-N$.

quote.quote: The source dimensions sum to $N$ and the sink dimensions to $Wm-N$.

children.claim: On a side wire joining neighbouring triples with indicators $t_X,t_Y$, the varying label component passes through $\langle t_X\rangle\subset t_Y^\perp\subset F$ (tensored with fixed factors), which is possible precisely because $t_X\perp t_Y$.

quote.quote: The first inclusion is possible because $t_X\perp t_Y$.

children.claim: Every edge joins comparable nondegenerate labels, and the only decreasing edges are the central-wire edges from time 3 to time 4, each losing dimension $h=100$, so $L$ is $100$ times the number of central wires over all invocations.

quote.quote: The only decreasing edges are the central-wire edges from time 3 to time 4; their dimension loss is $h$.

children.claim: Signed changes telescope at each gate, since each touched wire enters and leaves it with the same gate label, so they sum to $(Wm-N)-N=Wm-2N$; turning the signed losses on decreasing edges into absolute values adds $2L$.

quote.quote: The signed sum of dimension changes telescopes at every gate: each touched wire has one incoming and one outgoing incidence with the same gate label.

children.claim: Over $\mathbb F_2$ every nonzero edge residual (orthogonal complement of the smaller label in the larger) contains a vector of norm one, so it is nondegenerate and nonalternating and therefore has an orthonormal basis.

quote.quote: Thus every nonzero residual is nonalternating.

children.claim: The exact loss ratios are $L_{\rm b}/N=100/539$ and $L_{\rm c}/N=101/539$, both smaller than $1/2$.

quote.quote: In particular, both are smaller than $1/2$.

children.claim: In the bit network, assigning the projection $P_U$ (onto $U$ along $U^\perp$) to each gate or sink with label $U$, $-P_{U_a}$ to source $X_a$ and $0$ to other sources gives $M_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{source}(w)}=I_m$ on every role and total edge rank $s=s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}m-N+2L_{\rm b}<W_{\rm b}m$.
children.method: Read off the rank of each edge difference of projections from the label dimensions, and add the exceptional first edges at the sources separately.

motivation.text: For nested nondegenerate labels the difference of the two projections is itself a projection whose rank is the dimension change, so the label budget transfers to ranks, except on the edges where the negative source projection breaks this rule.

children.claim: For nondegenerate $U\subset V$, $P_V-P_U$ is the identity on $V\cap U^\perp$ and zero on its orthogonal complement, so its rank equals $\dim V-\dim U$, and reversing the edge only negates it.

quote.quote: Its rank is $\dim V-\dim U$; reversing the edge negates the matrix without changing its rank.

children.claim: The exceptions are the $N$ negative source projections: at stage 1 the first gate on $X_a$ has label $U_a$, so its first edge matrix is $P_{U_a}-(-P_{U_a})=2P_{U_a}$, of rank one where the dimension change is zero, adding $N$ to the rank sum.

quote.quote: Its first edge matrix is therefore $2P_{U_a}$, of rational rank one, where the corresponding dimension change was zero.

children.claim: Hence $s_{\rm b}=(W_{\rm b}m-2N+2L_{\rm b})+N$, whose deficit from $W_{\rm b}m$ is $N-2L_{\rm b}>0$ because $L_{\rm b}<N/2$.

quote.quote: Its deficit from $W_{\rm b}m$ is $N-2L_{\rm b}>0$.

children.claim: The negative source matrix is what makes the endpoint uniform: on $X_a$ the endpoint difference is $P_{U_a^\perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m$, and every other role has zero source and identity sink matrix.

quote.quote: For an input $X_a$ the endpoint difference is $P_{U_a^\perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m$.

children.claim: In the complex network with binary labels and phase frames $\mathcal C_U=H^{\otimes m}\operatorname{diag}_x(i^{\operatorname{wt}(P_Ux)\bmod 4})H^{\otimes m}$, each edge's frame change is a product of one translation kernel $aI+bX_v$ or its inverse per vector $v$ of an orthonormal basis of the edge residual, so the network needs $s=s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c}<W_{\rm c}m$ kernels in all.
children.method: Show that Hamming weight modulo four is additive over orthogonal binary vectors, so the phase of a residual factors into one two-valued character per orthonormal basis vector, and conjugate each character by Hadamard matrices into a translation kernel.

motivation.text: The phase $i^{\operatorname{wt}(P_Ux)}$ splits along an orthogonal decomposition only if weights add modulo four, which holds exactly when supports meet evenly, i.e. for orthogonal binary vectors; that is why orthonormal residual bases give one kernel per unit of dimension.

children.claim: Because $\operatorname{wt}(z+w)=\operatorname{wt}(z)+\operatorname{wt}(w)-2|\operatorname{supp}(z)\cap\operatorname{supp}(w)|$, weight is additive modulo $4$ when $z\cdot w=0$, so $q_V-q_U$ is a sum of one term $\operatorname{wt}(v)[v\cdot x]$ per orthonormal basis vector of the residual.

quote.quote: If $z\cdot w=0$, the intersection cardinality is even, so weight is additive modulo four.

children.claim: Each basis vector has odd weight, so it contributes a phase $i^{\pm[v\cdot x]}=\frac{1+i^{\pm1}}2+\frac{1-i^{\pm1}}2(-1)^{v\cdot x}$, and $H\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)H=X$ turns it into $aI+bX_v$ or its inverse.

quote.quote: The displayed phase therefore becomes $aI+bX_v$ or its inverse.

children.claim: A zero residual uses the empty basis, so the kernel count equals the absolute label budget $W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c}$ with no exceptional source term, a deficit of $2N-2L_{\rm c}>0$.

quote.quote: The deficit is $2N-2L_{\rm c}>0$.

children.claim: The relative deficits $1-s_{\rm b}/(W_{\rm b}m)=339/22587335000000$ and $1-s_{\rm c}/(W_{\rm c}m)=73/19906842167500$ both exceed $20\cdot2^{-50}$, and $m<2^{20}$ gives $\log m<20$, so $m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20\cdot2^{-50})$ and hence $s_{\rm b}/W_{\rm b}<m^{\tau}$ and $s_{\rm c}/W_{\rm c}<m^{\sigma}$ with $\tau=\sigma=1-2^{-50}$.

quote.quote: Both exact deficits displayed above are greater than $20\cdot2^{-50}$.

children.claim: For a fixed rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ and two groups of $m$ fields over $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$ ($q$ a fixed odd prime avoiding all denominators), with every $H_i$ before every $D_j$, the shear $(H,D)\mapsto(H+AD,D)$ costs exactly $a$ interchanges of $b$-digit field pairs plus $O(V)$ work, so each edge of the bit network costs as many smaller interchanges as its rank.
children.method: Factor $A=E_1\Pi E_2$ with invertible lower-triangular $E_1,E_2$ and a partial permutation $\Pi$ with $a$ ones, apply the triangular factors as linear-time controlled shifts, and realise each one of $\Pi$ by a single interchange between two controlled updates.

motivation.text: Controlled shifts are linear-time only when the target field follows its controls, which is exactly what a lower-triangular change of coordinates needs; the factorization pushes all non-triangular work into the $a$ ones of $\Pi$.

quote.quote: Lower triangular changes of coordinates can be performed entirely in this direction.

children.claim: Eliminating from the topmost nonzero row with its rightmost nonzero pivot uses only lower-triangular operations and isolates one rank-one block per step, giving $A=E_1\Pi E_2$ with exactly $a$ ones in $\Pi$ (a Bruhat factorization in reversed coordinate order).

quote.quote: Each step isolates a rank-one block and leaves the remaining rank in the active submatrix.

children.claim: A lower-triangular transformation of $H$ or of $D$ costs $O(V)$: update coordinates in descending physical order, each by a unit multiple plus a fixed combination of earlier, still unchanged coordinates.

quote.quote: A lower triangular transformation of $H$, or of $D$, costs $O(V)$: update coordinates in descending physical order.

children.claim: Each one of $\Pi$ at $(i,j)$, i.e. $H_i\gets H_i+D_j$, is done as $D_j\gets D_j+H_i$, one interchange of $(H_i,D_j)$, and $D_j\gets H_i-D_j$, so the number of recursive interchanges is exactly the rank $a$.

quote.quote: In particular, the number of recursive calls is the rational rank $a$; temporary tapes used for the other operations do not multiply that count.

children.claim: One fixed-tape procedure transforms any bit array on $[P]\times[2^u]\times[G]\times[2^u]\times[B]$ by $(p,h,g,d,z)\mapsto(p,d,g,h,z)$ in $O(Vu^{\tau})$ steps, with $\tau=1-2^{-50}$.
children.method: Prove the bound for power widths with enough rows by running the bit network on role streams, then supply rows from high digits, split a general width into base-$m$ pieces, and pad binary chunks to radix $q$.

motivation.text: The network recursion needs a row field divisible by $W^k$ and widths that are powers of $m$; borrowing a few high digits as rows and summing base-$m$ pieces meets both requirements at a cost below the final bound.

quote.quote: Rows for a general array can be supplied by a few of its own high digits.

children.salient: The final effect is an exact permutation of addresses, yet the procedure forms XOR combinations of the data along the way, and that is what lets it beat moving the $u$ bits one at a time.

children.claim: If $s/W<m^{\tau}$, two disjoint chunks of $e=m^k$ radix-$q$ digits each, preceded by a row field whose length is divisible by $W^k$, can be interchanged in $O(Ve^{\tau})$ time on a fixed number of tapes, preserving all other fields.
children.method: Split whole rows cyclically into $W$ role streams, run the bit network with frames $\Phi_M:(H,D)\mapsto(H+MD,D)$ so that every role ends with the shear $H\gets H+D$, implement each edge shear by recursive interchanges of $e/m$-digit fields, and solve the recurrence $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$.

motivation.text: Splitting whole rows gives all role streams the same address set, which the frame identity needs, and makes every recursive call act on only $1/W$ of the volume, so the rank count $s$ enters the cost only through $s/W$.

quote.quote: The row split supplies the common address set used in the frame identity~\eqref{eq:common-frame-identity}.

children.claim: Cyclically splitting whole rows into $W$ role streams within each prefix gives streams with the same remaining shape, including full ranges of $H$ and $D$, each of logical volume $V/W$ and with row count divisible by $W^{k-1}$.

quote.quote: Each has logical volume $V/W$, and its row count is divisible by $W^{k-1}$.

children.claim: Since $\Phi_{M'}\Phi_M=\Phi_{M'+M}$ commutes with pointwise XOR gates, the frame identity and $M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}=I_m$ give $\Phi_{I_m}$, i.e. $H\gets H+D$, on every original row after merging, scratch rows with arbitrary contents included.

quote.quote: The result is $H\leftarrow H+D$ on every original row, including rows assigned to scratch roles, whose initial values were arbitrary.

children.claim: The updates $D\gets D-H$, $H\gets H+D$, $D\gets H-D$ interchange the chunks; only the middle shear uses the network, the other two are linear-time controlled updates.

quote.quote: The transformation sends $(H,D)$ to $(D,H)$.

children.claim: The node makes exactly $s$ recursive calls (the sum of edge ranks), each on a role stream of volume $V/W$, plus $O(V)$ work, so $F_0=O(1)$ and $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$.

quote.quote: The number of recursive calls is the sum of the edge ranks, exactly $s$.

children.claim: With $s/W<m^{\tau}$ the geometric sum $\sum_{j\le k}(s/W)^j$ is $O(m^{k\tau})$, whether $s/W\le1$ or not, so $F_k=O(e^{\tau})$.

quote.quote: Hence $F_k=O(e^\tau)$.

children.claim: Parking the inactive role streams on a stack and reusing the same tapes at every depth costs $O(V)$ per node, so temporary storage does not enter the factor $s/W$.

quote.quote: Temporary storage is therefore not substituted for logical volume in the factor $s/W$.

children.claim: For chunks of $e$ radix-$q$ digits, borrowing the top $O(\log e)$ digits of both chunks as a row field of range at least $W^k$, padding the row count, and splitting the remaining width into base-$m$ pieces gives an interchange in $O(Ve^{\tau})$; padding binary ranges $[2^u]$ to $[q^e]$ then gives $O(Vu^{\tau})$.
children.method: Exchange and join the high digits to form rows, apply the power-width interchange to each base-$m$ piece, then undo the joins, the row padding and the radix padding.

motivation.text: The power-width procedure needs a row field and widths that are powers of $m$; high digits supply rows at only $O(V\log e)$ movement cost, and a base-$m$ expansion with digits below $m$ makes the piece costs a geometric sum dominated by its top term.

children.claim: Exchanging and joining the high digits costs $O(V\log e)$, and padding the row count to a multiple of $W^k$ less than doubles the volume.

quote.quote: Exchanging and joining the high parts costs $O(V\rho)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:elementary-streams}.

children.claim: Writing the remaining width as $\sum_ja_jm^j$ with $a_j<m$, the pieces cost $O(V)\sum_ja_jm^{j\tau}=O(Ve^{\tau})$ because $m^k<me$.

quote.quote: The fixed bound $a_j<m$ and the inequality $m^k<me$ make this a geometric sum of the stated order.

children.claim: Padding each binary range $[2^u]$ to $[q^e]$ with $q^e\ge2^u$ preserves order and raises the volume by less than the fixed factor $q^2$, and $e=O(u)$, so the interchange costs $O(Vu^{\tau})$.

quote.quote: Since $e=O(u)$ for fixed $q$, the bound is $O(Vu^\tau)$.

children.claim: For records that are polynomials of length $r=2^{\Theta(p/d)}$ with disk-valued coefficients on the grid $2^{-p}\mathbb Z[i]$, $d=\Theta(p^{\epsilon})$ and $K=\lfloor d^c\rfloor$, the tensor product $\mathcal H$ of $H_0$ on one selected bit in each of $D\le d$ consecutive $K$-bit chunks, followed by one truncation $Q_p$, costs $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ with $\lambda'=1-2^{-54}$ and has error below $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$.
children.method: Realise $C^{\otimes D}$ by the complex network with phase frames, implement its binary basis changes by packed selected-bit additions, split rows among roles to get a volume recurrence, evaluate exactly with guard bits, and convert to $H_0^{\otimes D}$ by diagonal phases.

motivation.text: Doing the $D$ butterflies one at a time costs $D$ full passes; the network recursion replaces this by a power $d^{\lambda'}$, and exact evaluation with one final truncation keeps the error of a whole layer at a single rounding.

quote.quote: whereas separate butterfly factors would require $D$ whole-array passes.

children.salient: All $D$ butterflies of a layer together cost less than $D$ passes, $O(d^{\lambda'})$ with $\lambda'<1$, and the whole layer incurs only one rounding.

children.claim: On a group of $e=mf$ selected bits arranged in $m$ slots of $f$ bits, the complex network with phase frames applies $C^{\otimes e}$, where $C=aI+bX$ with $a=(1+i)/2$, $b=(1-i)/2$, on every role using exactly $s_{\rm c}$ forward child calls on the $f$ bits of one slot plus a fixed number of binary row additions and exact Gaussian-dyadic scalar operations; and $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$ recovers the normalized butterflies.
children.method: Conjugate each edge's product of translation kernels by an invertible binary change of basis so that the kernels act on whole slots, turn inverse kernels into forward ones with $Z$ signs and fourth-root phases, and telescope the frames to $C^{\otimes m}$ on every role.

motivation.text: A translation kernel in a general direction $v$ is not a slot operation, but after a basis change that makes $v$ a coordinate vector it acts on one slot, where it is a smaller instance of the same layer; the basis change itself only XORs address bits.

children.claim: By the complex interface, an edge frame change is $\prod_j(aI+bX_{v_j})^{\epsilon_j}$ over an orthonormal basis of its residual, so the number of directional kernels is the residual dimension, also on decreasing edges.

quote.quote: The number of directional kernels is precisely $\rho_{\rm edge}$, including on decreasing edges.
